message: The operation completed successfully.
Incorrect function.
The system cannot find the file specified.
The system cannot find the path specified.
Access is denied.
hint: Check NTFS and share permissions, the account the process runs as, and whether the token is elevated.

message: The handle is invalid.
Not enough memory resources are available to process this command.
The data is invalid.
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
hint: Use Resource Monitor or handle.exe to find the process holding the file open.

message: The request is not supported.
The network path was not found.
hint: Usually name resolution or a firewall blocking TCP 445, rather than permissions.

message: The network name cannot be found.
The parameter is incorrect.
There is not enough space on the disk.
The data area passed to a system call is too small.
The specified module could not be found.
hint: A dependency DLL is missing. Dependency Walker or Process Monitor will name it.

message: Cannot create a file when that file already exists.
Is not a valid Win32 application.
hint: Commonly a 32-bit or 64-bit architecture mismatch.

message: The service did not respond to the start or control request in a timely fashion.
The service cannot be started because it is disabled or has no enabled devices associated with it.
The specified service does not exist as an installed service.
The service did not start due to a logon failure.
hint: Check the service account password and its Log on as a service right.

message: Multiple connections to a server or shared resource by the same user, using more than one user name, are not allowed.
hint: Run net use * /delete and reconnect with a single credential.

message: A specified logon session does not exist. It may already have been terminated.
A required privilege is not held by the client.
hint: The account is missing a user right such as SeBackupPrivilege — check local or group policy.

message: The user name or password is incorrect.
Account restrictions are preventing this user from signing in.
hint: Blank passwords, logon hour limits or workstation restrictions all surface here.

message: The password for this account has expired.
This user account has been disabled.
The specified domain either does not exist or could not be contacted.
Logon failure: the user has not been granted the requested logon type at this computer.
hint: The account lacks Allow log on locally, or Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services.

message: The Windows Installer service could not be accessed.
User cancelled installation.
Fatal error during installation.
hint: The generic MSI failure. The real cause is in the verbose log: msiexec /i package.msi /l*v install.log.

message: This action is only valid for products that are currently installed.
Another installation is already in progress. Complete that installation before proceeding with this install.
This installation package could not be opened.
Another version of this product is already installed.
Invalid command line argument.
The requested operation completed successfully. The system will need to be restarted so the changes can take effect.
hint: Exit code 3010 is a success, not a failure. Deployment tools that treat it as an error will retry forever.

message: Not implemented.
No such interface supported.
Invalid pointer.
Operation aborted.
Unspecified error.
hint: The least specific error in Windows. Treat it as a prompt to read the component's own log.

message: Catastrophic failure.
Not enough memory resources are available to complete this operation.
The parameter is incorrect.
The service cannot be started because it is disabled.
hint: The Windows Update service (wuauserv) has been disabled, often by a hardening baseline.

message: This operation returned because the timeout period expired.
The source files could not be found.
hint: Point DISM at a mounted install.wim with /Source:wim:<path>:1 /LimitAccess.

message: The source files could not be downloaded.
hint: Common when enabling .NET 3.5 or another Feature on Demand without a source. Supply /Source or allow access to Windows Update.

message: The installation of the update failed.
hint: Very often too little free space in the System Reserved partition, or a VPN blocking the update endpoints.

message: Operation failed for all the updates.
The update server returned HTTP 503, service unavailable.
hint: Usually the WSUS application pool has stopped. Check IIS on the WSUS server.

message: The proxy server or target server name cannot be resolved.
hint: Classic WSUS misconfiguration: check the WUServer policy value and the client's proxy settings.

message: The application was reported as installed successfully, but the detection rule did not find it afterwards.
hint: The install succeeded and the detection rule is wrong. Check the file path, version comparison or registry key you used to detect it.

message: The remediation failed.
hint: Seen on Intune app and policy remediations. The device-side detail is in the IntuneManagementExtension log.

message: The instruction referenced memory it could not access.
hint: A crash rather than a permissions problem, despite the name.

message: An invalid parameter was passed to a service or function.
A process has requested access to an object but has not been granted those access rights.
The object name is not found.
The path does not exist.
The specified account does not exist.
hint: In event 4625 this distinguishes a bad username from a bad password, which is 0xC000006A.

message: The user name is correct but the password is wrong.
hint: A run of these against one account in event 4625 is a password-spray signature.

message: The attempted logon is invalid, due to either a bad user name or authentication information.
The user account has restrictions that prevent this logon.
The user account has time restrictions and cannot sign in at this time.
The user account is restricted and cannot be used to sign in from this computer.
The user account password has expired.
The user account is currently disabled.
The program cannot start because a required DLL was not found.
The user account has expired.
The user must change their password before signing in for the first time.
The user account has been automatically locked because too many invalid logon attempts were made.
